summary: Iteration 2 revision testing (frontend-only, no backend). Ran end-to-end Playwright tests for all 11 revised features: Welcome Back popup with service-wise groups + 5MB note, service detail expected-completion + Required/Uploaded sections, callback modal selection-summary + Change flow with expert auto-swap, invoice tax-format view + PDF download, forgot-password full flow with persisted password + subsequent login, complaint tracking with Track Ticket ID -> /ticket/:id page (5-stage stepper + all sections), feedback rating response screens (1-star sad + 5-star positive) both with 'View Recommended Services' -> /recommended navigation. Found 1 critical bug (missing useNavigate in ComplaintModal) which I fixed. After fix: 100% of automated checks passed.

ui_bugs.issue: ReferenceError: 'navigate is not defined' — Track Ticket ID button threw error because useNavigate() hook was never called inside ComplaintModal, causing the click to no-op / crash and user was left on dashboard instead of /ticket/:id. FIXED by adding `const navigate = useNavigate();` inside ComplaintModal.

action_items: Review the applied fix in /app/frontend/src/oli/modals.jsx (added useNavigate hook inside ComplaintModal).

TEST 2 large-file (>5MB) rejection could not be automated via Playwright because the file input is dynamically created inside pickFile() and immediately clicked; the 5MB validation code path is present in useUploadFlow (modals.jsx) and reviewed by inspection. Recommend manual verification.
How-to-Use tour, chatbot, mobile 375px checks were not fully automated but no console errors detected on dashboard.
critical_code_review_comments: modals.jsx is 581 lines — consider splitting per-modal into separate files for maintainability.

Multiple modals rely on `document.querySelector('.fixed.z-[70]')` implicit z-index for stacking; the Welcome Back modal and later ConfirmModal share the same z, which can cause pointer-events interception during automated tests (not a user issue but flaky for tests).
